extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH grant applications (PD/PI) — specifically the Human Subjects, Protocol Synopsis, Vertebrate Animal Section, Select Agent, and Resource Sharing Plan sections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for NIH grant application sections covering human subjects protection, protocol synopsis (clinical trial descriptors), vertebrate animal use, select-agent laboratory capabilities, and resource sharing. The page lists required fields, justifications, and operational standards investigators must provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of specimens and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens and data will remain confidential. Specimens and data will be labeled with a numerical code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coded identifiers (numerical code) to protect participant confidentiality. Ensure labeling practices preserve confidentiality of subject-identifiable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidental findings expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the nature of the study, no incidental findings are expected to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether incidental findings are expected; if none, explicitly declare that. If expected, describe plan to handle them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of vulnerable subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Special groups (pregnant females, fetuses, the elderly, children, prisoners and the cognitively impaired, etc.) will be excluded from this protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify vulnerable populations and justify inclusion or exclusion. If excluded, list groups explicitly; if included, provide additional protections and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential benefits to participants and society
rubrics_metrics.description: For study participants, both the anticipated risks and benefits are very low. Society is expected to gain a long-term benefit from the results of this study, related to discovery of novel countermeasures against filoviruses and arenaviruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe both individual participant benefits (direct or none) and broader societal/knowledge benefits. Be explicit about expected magnitude and nature of benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of knowledge to be gained
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no direct benefits to the individual subject, but expected long-term benefits to society include improved treatment of patients with filovirus and arenavirus infection. Thus, the potential benefits to society are high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the importance and potential impact of the knowledge to be generated, especially when direct participant benefit is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design — detailed description
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis (Study 1) — Detailed Description (field present to describe study design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, detailed description of study design sufficient for review, including procedures, timing, and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design — primary purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis field: Primary Purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the primary purpose of the study (e.g., treatment, prevention, diagnostic, supportive care, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Interventions — Type, Name, Description (fields to specify interventions used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each intervention list type (drug/device/behavioral), commercial or investigational name, and concise description of how it will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study phase indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Study Phase — Is this an NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trial? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate clinical trial phase clearly and answer NIH-defined Phase III question when applicable; follow NIH definitions for phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention model
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Intervention Model (field present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify allocation framework (e.g., parallel, crossover, factorial, single group) and justify choice relative to study objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking (blinding) specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Masking — Yes/No and which roles are masked (Participant, Care Provider, Investigator, Outcomes Assessor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare whether masking will be used and for which roles; describe procedures to maintain masking and how unmasking will be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Allocation (field present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how participants will be allocated to arms (randomization method, stratification, allocation ratio) and any concealment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Outcome Measures — Type, Name, Time Frame, Brief Description (fields to enumerate outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary and secondary outcomes with precise measurement definitions, timing, and clinically/research-relevant rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical design and power
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Statistical Design and Power (field present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statistical analysis plan and power/sample size calculations demonstrating adequacy to detect clinically meaningful effects; include assumptions and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject participation duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Subject Participation Duration (field present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State total duration each participant will be involved, including follow-up periods and rationale for timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA-regulated intervention and IND/IDE status
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Will the study use an FDA-regulated intervention? (Yes/No). If yes, describe availability of Investigational Product (IP) and IND/IDE status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using FDA-regulated products, state IND/IDE status, provide supporting documentation, and describe IP availability and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable clinical trial under FDAAA
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Is this an applicable clinical trial under FDAAA? (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine and state whether the trial meets FDAAA definition; plan for required registration and reporting if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol Synopsis: Dissemination Plan (field present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for sharing results (publications, data repositories, registration), timelines, and mechanisms to ensure public access per NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed onset studies reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Delayed Onset Studies — field to list Delayed Onset Studies; example: 'The form does not have any delayed onset studies' and 'Anticipated Clinical Trial? Justification'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether delayed onset enrolment will occur and justify anticipated clinical trial status; provide rationale if no delayed onset studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of animals and how they will be used (VAS Point 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide species, supplier, strain choice, age choice, sex distribution, and detailed use (e.g., numbers for toxicity, PK, infection/challenge studies). Example: suppliers (The Jackson Laboratory), BALB/c mice, 4–5-week old, 50:50 female:male ratio, detailed group sizes for experimental needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List supplier, strain justification, age, sex distribution and exact experimental procedures, dosing regimens, sampling time points, and numbers per group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for the use of animals (VAS Point 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify why animals are necessary: no acceptable alternatives, species suitability, prior evidence of susceptibility, and consideration of ABSL4 space and cost. Example text: 'The use of animals is justified by the fact that the course of MARV infection and affect of antiviral treatment...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why non-animal alternatives are insufficient, why chosen species is appropriate, and how animal use is minimized consistent with scientific objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of discomfort, distress, pain, and injury (VAS Point 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures to minimize pain/distress: sedation/anesthesia for procedures, monitoring clinical signs (ruffled hair, hunch back, inappetence, weight loss, decreased movement), euthanasia criteria if 2 signs met or labored breathing or veterinarian judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify anesthesia/analgesia regimens, clinical monitoring schedules, objective humane endpoints, staff training, and decision rules for euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia methods and criteria (VAS Point 4 and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe euthanasia methods (e.g., cervical dislocation under isoflurane anesthesia for rats; CO2 chamber with specified flow rates for mice; immediate euthanasia for severe signs) and compliance with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide humane euthanasia methods consistent with AVMA Guidelines, include verification of death procedures (observation of respiration, chest palpation), and state circumstances for immediate euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC approvals and institutional assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: State that SOPs and IACUC applications have been filed and approved (e.g., IACUC application #1706MU approved; institutional animal welfare assurance number D16-00048).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include IACUC protocol numbers, institutional assurance numbers, and attest that procedures conform to approved protocols and institutional oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal numbers and minimization of group sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide total animal numbers and breakdown (e.g., total of 1,080 mice: 540 males + 540 females) and justification that numbers are minimum consistent with scientific objectives and statistical calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present exact animal counts by sex/group, and justify numbers with statistical reasoning and strategies to minimize animal use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacokinetic (PK) study design for animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe PK procedures: dosing routes (IV/IT), time points (up to eight over 24 hours), sample sizes per time point (n=3), and total number of mice (e.g., 192 over two years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sampling schedule, analytical methods (e.g., LC-MS/MS), and rationale for time points and sample sizes to define PK parameters (Cmax, AUC, half-life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of pain/distress and enrichment (Alliance study)
rubrics_metrics.description: All procedures designed to minimize discomfort; animals fed and watered, cages contain nestlet enrichment; attending veterinarian reviews protocols and analgesic/anesthetic regimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include environmental enrichment, routine animal care, and AV/Veterinarian consultation details; document IACUC categorization of pain/distress levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — authorized agents and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: List BSL4 agents licensed for use in proposal (Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, mouse-adapted Marburg) and authorized personnel (CDC-registered PI, staff with >5–9 years experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific select agents to be used, list personnel authorized and their credentials/registration, and provide their experience and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — registration and responsible official
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration status of entities where Select Agent(s) will be used: Texas Biomed is a select agent registered entity with HHS/CDC and USDA; registration certificate and number provided; Responsible Official (RO) and Alternate RO exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registration documentation, RO contact, and demonstrate compliance with 42 CFR 73 and Select Agent Program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — facility features, containment and redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities where select agent work will be used: ABSL4 full-suit lab with multiple airlocks, HEPA filtration, decontamination airlocks, emergency exit/decontamination chamber, redundant mechanical systems and emergency power, intrusion detection and secured access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail containment levels, access controls, air handling, decontamination systems, mechanical redundancy, and emergency power to demonstrate appropriate biosafety/biocontainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — equipment and capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: List specialized equipment available in ABSL4: biosafety hoods, incubators, centrifuges, -80°C freezers, autoclave, analyzers (hematology, coagulation), telemetry systems, necropsy/procedure areas, and animal housing capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document on-site capabilities to perform proposed work safely and to support sample analysis and animal monitoring in high containment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — SOPs, training and compliance with BMBL/NIH/CDC guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ABSL4 Operations and Safety Manuals specify policies, procedures, and SOPs that comply with applicable Federal/State regulations and 'Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories' guidelines. Employees are trained from these manuals and project-specific SOPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of written SOPs, training programs, and adherence to BMBL/NIH/CDC guidance; document training records where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — inventory, storage, and disposal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Infectious cultures and inventory stocks are stored inside ABSL4 in locked refrigerators/freezers; electronic Inventory (eInventory) documents usage; containers labeled with agent identity, date, and barcode; materials to be discarded are placed in disinfectant-filled sealable containers and autoclaved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe inventory tracking, labeling, secure storage conditions, leak-proof transport containers, disinfectant/disposal procedures, and autoclave use for waste management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agents — transfer and possession controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Select agent use, transfer or possession is forbidden without RO permission and required forms and written approval from CDC Select Agent Program. ABSL4 investigators must also submit application to Biohazard and Safety Committee for approval prior to BSL4 work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe administrative controls for authorization, transfer paperwork, RO approvals, and institutional committee review prior to select agent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel monitoring and communications in ABSL4
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel in lab are continuously monitored and communicate through a scrambled UHF communication system worn inside the suit; critical parameters (air flow, pressure differentials, breathing air) are continuously monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document systems for real-time monitoring of personnel, environmental parameters, and communications to ensure safety and rapid emergency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan — data and materials sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fox Chase Chemical Diversity Center is committed to rapidly sharing data, following NIH guidelines. After filing patents if appropriate, data will be prepared and submitted for publication in scholarly journals. Peer reviewed publications will be submitted to publicaccess@nih.gov according to required time parameters. Project resources will be made available per NIH policy; materials will be distributed to collaborators and filled in a timely fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete plans for data sharing, publication submission to NIH public access, material distribution policies, timelines, and any constraints (e.g., patenting) affecting sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing disclosures — model organisms and GWAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing model organisms: No model organisms will be generated. Genome-wide association studies: No genome-wide association studies will be performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly whether model organisms will be generated or GWAS performed and provide sharing plans if applicable.
